subject: general
question: Which Constitutional Amendment Bill, introduced in the Lok Sabha in 2025, seeks to provide for the removal of the Prime Minister, Chief Minister, or any Minister who remains in custody for 30 consecutive days for a serious criminal offence?

options.text: The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2025
The Constitution (One Hundred and Thirtieth Amendment) Bill, 2025
The Constitution (One Hundred and Twenty-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2025
The Constitution (One Hundred and Thirty-First Amendment) Bill, 2025

solution:
The correct answer is __**The Constitution (One Hundred and Thirtieth Amendment) Bill, 2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Constitution (One Hundred and Thirtieth Amendment) Bill, 2025** was introduced in the **Lok Sabha** during the **Budget Session** of **2025** to address a significant legal vacuum regarding the eligibility of ministers to hold office while in judicial custody.
 
• The primary objective of this bill is to provide for the **automatic removal** of a **Prime Minister**, **Chief Minister**, or any **Minister** at the Union or State level if they remain in **custody** for a period of **30 consecutive days** or more.
 
• The bill specifically targets situations where these high-ranking officials are arrested for a **serious criminal offence**, ensuring that the administrative machinery of the country or a state does not come to a standstill due to the incarceration of its executive head.
 
• Under the proposed amendment, the **30-day** threshold is considered a definitive period after which the individual is deemed unable to perform their constitutional duties, thereby necessitating their **removal** from the **Council of Ministers**.
